title: Significance status board
description: A board answers one question across several results at once — 'are these real?' — in claim-state terms. It holds no evidence of its own: every row either links a record, which is where evidence lives, or quotes a source directly. It is a separate schema rather than a record variant precisely so it cannot accumulate evidence fields and quietly become a second, weaker kind of record. Word caps, verdict language, and the row rule are enforced by `significance validate`, not by this schema alone.

kind.description: Discriminator. `significance validate` reads this to decide which schema a file answers to, so a board and a record can sit in the same directory without either being checked against the wrong one.

as_of.description: When the board as a whole was last gone over. Distinct from each row's own as_of, which may be older: a board reviewed today may contain a row nobody has revisited in a month, and collapsing the two would present the stale row as fresh.

parties.description: Same rule as a record: every asserted_by on this board must resolve to a key declared here, enforced by the validator.

row_state.description: `recorded` means somebody has done the work of finding out what this row says. `placeholder` means the row exists and nobody has. The distinction is load-bearing: a placeholder row may carry no claim and no status at all, so the board cannot present an unresearched result as though it had been looked at.

result.description: The result's name. On a placeholder row this carries a [FILL] marker, and the validator requires it to, so a half-finished row cannot look finished.

record.description: The record_id this row links, or null where no record exists yet. Not a foreign key the schema can check — records live in files, and a board may legitimately be built before them.

claim.description: The claim as the source states it, quoted. A row that links no record must have one, or the row asserts something on nobody's authority.

artifacts.description: Links, or [FILL] markers where the value is not yet known. Plain strings rather than URLs, because a [FILL] marker is not a URI and the renderer decides what may become a link (see safe_href).

then.description: A placeholder row carries no assertions. This is what stops the board fabricating a claim or a status for a result nobody has researched.

row_status.description: The same three questions the record-page strip answers, at row scale: what has been checked, what has not, as of when. Attributed as one block, because the three are a single reading by a single person at a single time.
